selection_method: Human-readable AI close reading; selectors locate already selected passages and do not extract assertions.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: An RDF graph G is a set of RDF triples; equality of G is equality of membership.
mappings.limitations: Concepts supplies the term domains; their concrete lexical constraints remain open.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: An ordinary RDF triple has subject in IRI or Blank, predicate in IRI, and object in IRI or Literal or Blank.
mappings.limitations: Disjoint syntactic categories are enforced. IRI and Literal are abstract domains, not validated concrete strings.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A generalized triple permits any RDF term in each of its three positions; a generalized graph is a set of generalized triples.
mappings.limitations: Ordinary graphs embed into generalized graphs. Instance and interpolation claims for generalized syntax have not been discharged.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: The empty graph contains no triples.
H is a subgraph of G exactly when every member of H is a member of G.
G is ground exactly when no blank node occurs in any triple of G.
For every set G, G union G equals G; repeated occurrences of a triple in an input list denote the same set as one occurrence.
mappings.limitations: This is a mathematical consequence of the set definition, not a separately labelled W3C rule.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: The union of G and H contains a triple exactly when G or H contains that triple, preserving blank-node identity.
mappings.limitations: Binary union; arbitrary families are not yet implemented.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: The binary merge of G and H takes their union after placing their blank nodes in disjoint copies. I satisfies that merge exactly when I satisfies G and I satisfies H.
mappings.limitations: Uses Sum B₁ B₂ for fresh identities. This is a representative up to blank-node renaming; literal equality to union for already-disjoint domains is not asserted.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For any G and H with a common blank-node domain, their union simply entails their merge.
mappings.limitations: Semantic consequence only. The stated syntactic instance relation and no-shared-nodes equality remain open.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: IR is a nonempty set of resources.
mappings.limitations: IR and IP are predicates on an ambient type U; no finiteness assumption.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: IP is a set of properties, permitted to overlap IR.
mappings.limitations: No IP subset IR constraint is imposed in simple interpretations.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For every p in IP, IEXT(p) is a set of pairs of elements of IR.
mappings.limitations: Subtype membership proofs express the domain and codomain restrictions.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For every IRI i, IS(i) belongs to IR union IP.
mappings.limitations: The source IRI domain is an abstract parameter.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: IL is a partial function from literals to IR.
mappings.limitations: Option encodes undefinedness. It does not identify literals with their denoted values.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For names, [I+A] agrees with IS on IRIs and IL on literals.
mappings.limitations: The function is Option-valued because IL is partial.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A triple s p o is true under [I+A] exactly when p denotes a property and s and o denote resources whose pair belongs to IEXT of that property.
mappings.limitations: Undefined denotation makes the existential truth condition false.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A ground graph G is true exactly when every triple of G is true under I; no blank-node assignment is needed.
mappings.limitations: GraphTrue also evaluates non-ground graphs under a specified A. ground_satisfaction proves agreement for ground graphs.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: If IL(l) is undefined, any triple containing l in any position is false, and any graph containing that triple is false.
mappings.limitations: Covers generalized positions as well as ordinary object literals.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Every simple interpretation satisfies the empty graph.
mappings.limitations: Extension preservation follows when extensions retain the same Satisfies relation and admit empty syntax.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A maps exactly the blank nodes occurring in G to IR. [I+A] agrees with A on those blank nodes and with I on names.
mappings.limitations: A partial ambient-domain function plus exact-domain condition represents the source's function on a subset. Restriction proves that unused extra assignments do not affect satisfaction.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: I satisfies G exactly when one assignment A of G's blank nodes makes every triple in G true.
mappings.limitations: The existential assignment quantifier is outside the universal triple quantifier.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A blank-node assignment is a witness to graph truth and is not a component of the simple interpretation I.
mappings.limitations: A structural modelling choice, not a separate theorem about all possible implementations.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: There exist an interpretation I and graphs G and H sharing a blank node such that I satisfies G and H separately and their merge, but I does not satisfy their union.
mappings.limitations: An abstract two-resource illustration of the informative discussion, not a transcription of the Alice/Bob drawing.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: I.Satisfies G is graph truth with an existential shared assignment. SimplySatisfiable G means some simple interpretation satisfies G; SimplyUnsatisfiable G is its negation. Every graph is simply satisfiable.
mappings.limitations: Universe-polymorphic in a fixed arbitrary carrier universe. Does not assert satisfiability in datatype-aware or RDF/RDFS regimes.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: G simply entails E exactly when every simple interpretation satisfying G also satisfies E.
mappings.limitations: Universe-polymorphic family: all carrier types U in a fixed arbitrary Lean universe u. No claim to quantify over all universes inside one Lean proposition.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: G and E are logically equivalent exactly when G simply entails E and E simply entails G.
For every graph G, including infinite graphs, there exists a simple interpretation satisfying G.
mappings.limitations: A one-element resource/property universe is a witness, not a restriction on the model class.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Every graph simply entails the empty graph; if the empty graph simply entails E then E is empty.
mappings.limitations: The proof works without finite graphs.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Every graph simply entails every subgraph of that graph.
If G is a subgraph of H and G simply entails E, then H simply entails E.
For an extension represented by additional conditions C on simple interpretations, simple entailment implies entailment under C.
mappings.limitations: Models only extensions over this graph syntax; does not formalize every permitted higher-level notation.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For ordinary graphs G and H, IsInstance H.generalize G.generalize implies H SimplyEntails G. More generally, every term substitution of an ordinary source G entails G; blank-to-blank renaming also works for generalized sources.
mappings.limitations: Complete instance-entails-original theorem for ordinary RDF endpoints, proved directly from truth conditions. The unrestricted generalized-source reading remains an open source question; IP ⊆ IR is not assumed. Generalized substitution entailment is now separately proved under RDFPropertyCondition, which forces IP ⊆ IR; this does not change the simple-entailment scope question.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Lists that denote equal sets of triples have the same graph identity and therefore the same Satisfies proposition.
mappings.limitations: Set identity is proved; a separately named general list-permutation satisfaction theorem is not yet provided.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: H is an IsInstance of G exactly when one partial Substitution μ replaces each selected blank consistently, leaving omitted blanks and all names fixed, and H is the set of resulting triples.
mappings.limitations: Shared ambient blank identities; the generalized syntax admits substitutions in every position. Use ordinary Graph endpoints when ordinary RDF syntax is required.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: IsInstance is reflexive and transitive. For a fixed μ, every triple in G.substitute μ is the image of a triple in G.
mappings.limitations: No finiteness or injectivity assumption; different triples may have the same image.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: InstanceWithVocabulary V H G requires an instance mapping whose name-valued replacements of occurring blanks lie in V; existing names need not lie in V.
mappings.limitations: V is a set of IRI-or-literal names, represented by Sum Iri Literal.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: ProperInstance H G has an instance mapping that replaces an occurring blank by a name, or maps two distinct occurring blanks to the same resolved term.
mappings.limitations: Only blanks occurring in G count; omitted replacements resolve to the unchanged blank. Proper instance does not mean proper subgraph.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: GraphIsomorphism G H supplies inverse blank renamings on the occurring blank nodes and a graph-image equality. The graphs are mutual instances and satisfy exactly the same simple interpretations.
mappings.limitations: A common ambient identity domain; unused identities need not be bijective. Isomorphism does not assert literal set equality or preservation of blank sharing with other graphs. A separately packaged Concepts bijection over all graph nodes remains to be provided.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: LeanGraph G means that every instance H of G that is a subgraph of G equals G: no instance is a proper subgraph.
mappings.limitations: Lean here is the RDF mathematical property, unrelated to the name of the proof assistant.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Every ground G is a LeanGraph. For ordinary graphs G and H, if H is both an instance and a subgraph of G, the graphs are LogicallyEquivalent.
mappings.limitations: Does not prove existence of lean subgraphs, or the source’s entire informal redundancy discussion; no generalized instance theorem is assumed.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For an ordinary conclusion E and any generalized premise G, G SimplyEntails E.generalize exactly when an instance of E.generalize is a subgraph of G. A Herbrand interpretation proves necessity; existing ordinary instance entailment proves sufficiency.
mappings.limitations: Both directions are proved for ordinary conclusions, without finiteness. Necessity also holds for generalized conclusions; the unrestricted generalized converse remains a source-scope question. One common ambient blank identity type is used.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For a ground conclusion E, G SimplyEntails E exactly when E is a subset of G.
mappings.limitations: Captures the ground-conclusion characterization, not an executable finite entailment decision procedure or the source complexity claim. No finiteness restriction on this theorem.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: If G SimplyEntails an ordinary E with a certified finite Enumeration, interpolation produces a finite instance H of E inside G, and H SimplyEntails E.
mappings.limitations: The conclusion is ordinary RDF; the premise may be generalized and infinite. Enumeration is the existing membership-faithful, duplicate-free finite representation; no graph finiteness axiom is introduced.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Name is Iri or Literal. Term.names includes a literal itself and its syntactic datatype IRI; a graph vocabulary is the union of the names contributed by its terms.
mappings.limitations: The total datatype : Literal → Iri projection is an explicit interface parameter. Concrete literal syntax, identity, lexical constraints and correctness of the supplied projection remain external obligations.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: If E contains IRI i in its vocabulary and G does not, G cannot SimplyEntail E. More strongly, entailment implies E.vocabulary is a subset of G.vocabulary.
mappings.limitations: Includes datatype IRI names via the supplied syntactic datatype projection. Applies to simple interpretations, not arbitrary stronger regimes.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A Skolemization supplies distinct IRIs for occurring blanks, fresh against G.vocabulary; its graph is the simultaneous substitution of all those blanks. The result is a ground, lean instance of G.
mappings.limitations: Freshness against G is formalized; global freshness at creation is an external naming obligation. The map is supplied, not proved to exist for arbitrary abstract IRI domains. This is full replacement as in Semantics §6, not the optional partial replacement of Concepts §3.5.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For an ordinary graph G, sk.graph SimplyEntails G.generalize by the existing substitution-entailment theorem.
mappings.limitations: Ordinary source; generalized-source claim remains scoped separately. This direction needs neither a nonempty blank set nor freshness/injectivity, although Skolemization supplies them where relevant.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: If G contains a blank node, G does not SimplyEntail sk.graph: the image contains a fresh IRI absent from G.
mappings.limitations: The nonempty-blank premise comes from the preceding source paragraph. This result also holds for generalized G; it concerns simple entailment only.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For ordinary G and H, if H avoids the fresh IRIs introduced by sk, sk.graph SimplyEntails H exactly when G SimplyEntails H. The inverse-name map turns an interpolation witness over sk.graph into one over G.
mappings.limitations: Ordinary graphs; no finiteness or disjoint-blank-domain premise. Avoidance includes datatype IRIs. The separate exact lifting equation H = sk(H′) remains open; no unrestricted commutation with substitutions is assumed.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A process relation is SimplyValid when every permitted input/output pair G,E satisfies SimplyEntails G E; SimplyInvalid is its negation. Valid processes compose and remain valid under additional interpretation conditions.
mappings.limitations: A relation models possible process outputs; this imposes no execution mandate. Separate syntax restrictions of an extension must still be respected.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Restricting simple interpretations by conditions C preserves every simple entailment and every SimplyValid process.
mappings.limitations: C retains the same Satisfies relation and graph syntax. The source also permits separate syntactic admissibility conditions, not represented by C; their satisfaction remains a separate obligation.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: RDFPropertyCondition states that x belongs to IP exactly when x is related by IEXT(I(rdf:type)) to I(rdf:Property). Its typed relation entails IP is a subset of IR.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: D is the set of datatype IRIs recognized by an interpretation; recognizing an IRI presupposes determining the unique datatype it identifies.
mappings.limitations: Parameterized by abstract IRI/literal domains and a fixed external datatype theory; concrete XSD, XML Char and BCP47 implementations are not supplied. Expert mapping review remains pending.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A recognized datatype IRI identifies the same externally specified datatype at every occurrence; the mechanism establishing that identification is outside this semantics.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A datatype supplies a lexical space and a partial lexical-to-value mapping; L2V selects that mapping and its range is the value space.
mappings.limitations: Parameterized by abstract IRI/literal domains and a fixed external datatype theory; concrete XSD, XML Char and BCP47 implementations are not supplied. Expert mapping review remains pending.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: A literal is ill-typed relative to D when its datatype IRI is recognized but its lexical form has no value under the corresponding mapping.
mappings.limitations: Parameterized by abstract IRI/literal domains and a fixed external datatype theory; concrete XSD, XML Char and BCP47 implementations are not supplied. Expert mapping review remains pending.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: RDF processors need not recognize datatype IRIs beyond rdf:langString and xsd:string; recognizing additional IRIs is permitted.
mappings.limitations: Required recognition is enforced for RDF models. Processor behavior and concrete datatype meaning are not verified.

Expert mapping review remains pending. ValueRealization is a partial injective representation of fixed values in a model carrier, not a new interpretation of the datatype IRI.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For each other IRI in D, its interpretation is the datatype it identifies.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For a literal typed with a recognized IRI other than rdf:langString, IL is the corresponding lexical-to-value result, including being undefined when that mapping is undefined.
mappings.limitations: Parameterized by abstract IRI/literal domains and a fixed external datatype theory; concrete XSD, XML Char and BCP47 implementations are not supplied. Expert mapping review remains pending.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Every graph containing an ill-typed literal is false in every D-interpretation; unrecognized datatype IRIs do not create this source of D-unsatisfiability.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: D-satisfiability means having at least one satisfying D-interpretation; S D-entails G when every D-interpretation satisfying S also satisfies G.

mappings.limitations: Parameterized by abstract IRI/literal domains and a fixed external datatype theory; concrete XSD, XML Char and BCP47 implementations are not supplied. Expert mapping review remains pending.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: RDFS domain or range consequences can force an individual into disjoint recognized datatype classes and thereby make a graph unsatisfiable.
mappings.limitations: If any shared term can be derived to inhabit two disjoint recognized datatype spaces, the whole graph is RDFS-unsatisfiable. This composes with domain/range and hierarchy rules; concrete integer/boolean disjointness remains a datatype-library obligation.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Ill-typed literals are the only source of unsatisfiability for simple D-entailment; adding RDF/RDFS vocabulary conditions can introduce other sources.
mappings.limitations: Constructs a D-model for every fixed external datatype theory and every graph without ill-typed literals, with no finiteness restriction. The carrier embeds all external values injectively and has one additional resource. This is an existence witness, not a new universal interpretation condition. Concrete RDF/RDFS model existence is a separate obligation.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Literals recognized to have the same value can be substituted in corresponding triples to obtain datatype entailments, including across different recognized datatypes with overlapping value spaces.
mappings.limitations: Simultaneous replacement is proved for every literal position, including across ordinary datatype spaces and normalized language-tagged values. Unchanged literals need no recognition proof. Different input triples may collapse to one set member. Concrete datatype value equalities remain external obligations.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: For a premise triple containing a literal typed by d in D, infer the generalized triple literal rdf:type d.
mappings.limitations: The rule and graph image use the source object-literal premise. The shared helper proves the stronger any-position semantic consequence. Recognized typing is required; well-typedness is not an extra premise. Both RDF and RDFS derivations preserve one assignment.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: The generalized RDF/RDFS closure of S towards E adds the prescribed finite-vocabulary axioms and saturates generalized triples with GrdfD1, rdfD2 and, for RDFS, rdfs1–rdfs13 at the base recognized datatype set.
mappings.limitations: Transcribes the conclusion-based axiom selection and base recognized set. The rdf:_1 fallback tests literal set growth after step 2, not merely absence of container IRIs in E. Saturation is an inductive least-closure specification; a finite executable generator and its equivalence are not yet proved. Completeness of the printed E-only selection is under review.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: If S is RDF-consistent, respectively RDFS-consistent, then S entails E in that regime exactly when the corresponding generalized closure towards E simply entails E.
mappings.limitations: Only the positive/sound direction is proved, including a concrete instance-subgraph criterion. The proof works for generalized endpoints, does not require consistency or finiteness, and retains one common assignment. No converse or complete algorithm is claimed. The printed container-axiom selection has an open source-scope question.

mappings.symbol_linked_english: Container vocabulary describes entities with a type and partial membership information; indexed membership properties distinguish positions, while rdfs:member is generic membership.
mappings.limitations: Proves that every indexed membership assertion entails generic rdfs:member membership through its full-family axiom, rdfs12 and rdfs7. Other container-description assertions remain unformalized; concrete IRI spelling is still an external vocabulary binding.
